chapter: Paul Barbarin and his own bands
title: Recent work with Paul Barbarin's small band
summary: Breaux recalls working with Barbarin's New Orleans-style band in recent years and who played in it, and the bassist who took his place.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Paul Barberin when he had a small New Orleans-style jazz band?
Except lately, of course. I mean, the last couple years ago you were with him.

Yeah, I worked with him a couple years ago on Clevester. Oh, he worked at Dream Room over at the Pier 600. He worked at Mardi Gras with him. And I worked at Paddock with him on the regular band off night. I don't think Paul ever worked at the Paddock regular. Who would be in the band? Oh, in Paul's band? Mm-hmm. He had Picky on trumpet. John Brunus, we call him Picky. And Trombone. The same trombone he's got now. Turbillon. Clemens Turbillon. And Willie Humphrey on clarinet. The same setup he's got now.
Yeah. Santiago. That's right. The San... Barnell on the... I mean, not Barnell. Black.
Leicester. That's his right there. Leicester, Santiago.
